newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH YEAR-END INFLATION AT 16.2 PCT - PENTOR POLL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH YEAR-END INFLATION AT 16.2 PCT - PENTOR POLL.

text.p: Polish bankers predict December year-on-year inflation to fall to 16.2 percent from 18.5 percent in 1996 and the zloty to be at 3.6000 against the dollar, a poll by the private Pentor institute showed.
"After a slight March-July fall in year-end inflation forecasts from 16.8 to 15.8 percent, bankers' predictions rose to 16.2 percent," the report said.
The report said 207 bankers polled in early August expected the dollar to end the year at 3.6000 zlotys, up from 3.4400 zlotys in the previous month's forecast.
All the bankers also see the central bank's lombard rate staying flat at 27 percent until the end of the year after a two-point rise in August.

The interest rate on credit for enterprises is expected to reach 24.8 percent at the end of the year, up 1.5 percentage point from July's forecast, and the three-month deposit rate 17.9 percent, up 1.1 percentage point.
The Pentor survey is commissioned monthly by the Polish Banking Association (ZBP).
